Towards a just solution in the Arabian Peninsula and the Gulf

#SeparateTheNameOfTheLandFromTheRule #PeacefulConstitutionForEqualCitizenship #NoToViolenceAndExclusion

In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate

We clearly call for separating the name of the land "Arabian Peninsula" from the name of any ruling family, and we demand peaceful constitutional reform that guarantees a state of law and equal citizenship for all Arabs, with our categorical rejection of violence and exclusion. This principle is the cornerstone of any just and sustainable solution.

Our region today is living through existential challenges that affect human life, dignity, and future. In light of the political and humanitarian crises suffered by the peoples of the Arabian Peninsula and the Gulf, the search for a just and peaceful solution has become an urgent necessity that cannot be delayed.

First: Diagnosis of the crisis

Wars, blockades, and the absence of political participation have led to widespread suffering affecting civilians. Continuation of this situation will only produce more division and instability. Therefore, the entry point to any solution begins with recognizing the right of all peoples to life, liberty, dignity, and security.

Second: On the language of discourse and 
identity awareness:

The land belongs to all: 
The Arabian Peninsula with its historic regions — Najd, Hejaz, Asir, and the Land of the Two Holy Mosques — is an Arab land belonging to all its inhabitants. Separating the identity of the land from the identity of any ruling authority strengthens the sense of common belonging and prevents symbolic monopoly.

Accuracy of description: 
When addressing public affairs, it is objective to attribute policies and decisions to the official bodies that issued them, far from generalization or insulting the population. This raises the level of discourse and serves awareness.

Inclusive Arabism: 
An Arab is one who belongs to the Arabic language and culture, regardless of his origin, religion, or color. This definition consolidates unity and blocks the path of exclusionary discourse.

Third: Features of a just solution And we reaffirm here again: 

There must be separation of the name of the land "Arabian Peninsula" from any family name, and moving forward toward peaceful constitutional reform that guarantees the rule of law and full equality in citizenship for all Arabs, with rejection of violence and exclusion in all its forms. This is the path that peoples aspire to and it is not achieved by violence nor by revenge:

Peaceful constitutional transformation: Calling for the establishment of constitutional systems in the countries of the Arabian Peninsula and the Gulf, based on the rule of law, separation of powers, peaceful transfer of power, and guaranteeing basic rights and freedoms for all citizens.

Legal civil activism: 
Forming peaceful civil movements that believe in dialogue and work by legal and diplomatic means to demand legitimate rights. We reject violence in all its forms, and we consider that peaceful struggle is the path guaranteed by all laws and international charters.

Building the civil state: 
Striving to build modern states based on equal citizenship, social justice, and sustainable development. A state that does not discriminate among its citizens, respects pluralism and protects human dignity.

Justice and accountability: 
Any excesses or violations must be subject to accountability before an independent and impartial judiciary. Justice does not mean revenge, but rather doing justice to victims and preventing recurrence of injustice, through fair public trials that guarantee the rights of all.

Fourth: An appeal to the inside and the world

We extend our hands to all peace-loving forces inside and outside. And we call upon the United Nations and the international community to support political solutions, lift suffering from civilians, and encourage comprehensive national dialogue that excludes no one.

The peoples of the region, with its Muslims, Christians, Jews and all its components, will not enjoy life, liberty, happiness and security except under systems that respect their will and preserve their dignity.

Conclusion:

In conclusion, we renew our firm call: The name of our land "Arabian Peninsula" must be separated from the name of any ruling family, and immediate work must be done for peaceful constitutional reform that consolidates the state of law and guarantees equal citizenship for all Arabs, under complete rejection of violence and exclusion. This is the path to true justice and lasting reconciliation.

Yes to a state of law and institutions
Yes to comprehensive national dialogue
Yes to transitional justice and reconciliation
No to war, violence and exclusion

Long live the will of free peoples
